t: Search the fragments of the golems. Report your findings to Semer Knef in the Swampy Pass.

While we sit here twiddling our thumbs, waiting for the next attack, I've got a proposal for you. There are bits and pieces of golems scattered all around here. Golems are phenomenal creations. A mechanism has been joined with them by magic, just like inside us, the Arisen.
From time to time the Junes enhanced the golems with combat magic and sometimes even powerful amulets!
You can find a lot of interesting stuff rooting around among the bits and pieces. We should do it. Better than letting all that go to waste. May Sarn guide your hand!
By the way, a dead golem might suddenly come to life if disturbed. So be careful.
So it's time for combat, eh? But what an interesting artifact! I'll have to study it carefully. But I'll do that when I get back to the camp. In any event, thank you.

We've got a little time now. I propose that we do not let it go to waste. There's another way we can help the fighters.
For as long as I've been here, every night I've heard the flapping of wings and the muffled sound of voices. For a while I had no idea what was happening. Then I noticed that the draconids were returning to the scene of the day's battle and were digging around for something. At first I thought that they were gathering the bodies of their comrades for some kind of foul farewell ritual. After a while I figured it out. They scour the field for the swords of fallen tribesmen.
Let's follow their example, only instead of following, let's go out before them and gather up all of their weapons so that they can't be used against us.
A weapon shouldn't be left out on the field. Every fighter knows this. And any way you look at it, the draconids are excellent fighters.

Wow! What a haul! It truly was a grand battle. Many draconids were slain.
We'll melt these swords down. Let the draconids arm themselves with sticks!
Promise Maria Zavetina that you will not use this new knowledge for evil.

Greetings. I did not think that I would be able to say this. But today I am glad that you are here with us, a hero whose fate is somehow so deeply intertwined with the fate of our world.
Your efforts could change the world. It's too bad you're not on our side. We - all of us - have made so many mistakes. There is a vast misunderstanding between us, Sarn's true children, and you, the heroes scrabbling about in the dust for the remnants of the old world. It will take a great deal of effort to mend this gap...
But now I quite simply have no one else to turn to. What's happening here on the Wandering Island is frightening. I do not hide that I am afraid. I beg you, promise me, before I put my faith in you, promise me that even if our paths part once again, that you will never use the knowledge we have given you for evil.
Fine. I... I believe you, although you are no friend of ours. My heart tells me that you are a creature of honor and that I can take you at your word.
Promise Maria Zavetina not to use this knowledge for evil.

Fine. I... I believe you, although you are no friend of ours. My heart tells me that you are a person of honor and that I can take you at your word.
Speak to the four infected cultists and report to Chaplain Maria Zavetina in the cultists' camp.

Listen to what I have to tell you. It pains us deeply to take you in, adherents to the dark god. And I am almost certain that one of you Nihazian lackeys is somehow involved!
"In what," you might ask? The camp is in a panic! A strange plague has struck scores of the daughters and sons of Sarn. The infected wither before your eyes and die in pain. But this is not a big deal - we can give them new bodies. The whole problem is that the Sparks of the sick do not remain near the body, nor do they go to the Purgatory. They simply disappear! It all began when you arrived here, with Nihaz's name on your lips! Who would you expect we suspected? Thankfully, we who walk the path of clarity shown to us by the merciful Sarn are not inclined to rash actions. The fact is, we don't have any proof.
I heard your oath and I heard of your successes in the Misty Lands. Your word is strong, and the poison of Nihaz's philosophy has not yet reached your soul. And I believe that you can help me!
We must find the cause and learn the nature of the illness. To start, I ask you to speak with the infected. I have already tried to speak with them, but I couldn't understand anything. Maybe you'll have better luck. Hurry, we could lose them at any moment.
Our doctor is a luminary in the world of science, a professor, and even he's clueless. He says it is the first time he's ever seen something like this.

So, what have we got? Not one of the sick knows how they were infected. Some were injured, while others are completely unharmed, but all of them are suffering from the same plague. What commonality is there among their histories? Ignatius Chernov! He's one of your fighters. He arrived here recently, just as you did: "They say Nihaz wants to make a pact with us."
I've been against that plan from the start! Nothing good will come of anyone who lets Nihaz into their heart. The dark god has no rules, except one: kill and betray!

Oh, I'm not sure... I can't say... We fought for three days and captured the Watchtower. You should have seen the assault - it was legendary! And not a scratch on me... I was that lucky! But later that night, in the camp... Ignatius Chernov... He offered to take a walk...
There are other things besides war, you know! Just one kiss, oh... I swear it! A single kiss... And that was it... When dawn broke I couldn't get up. A veil of darkness hung before my eyes. What's wrong with me? Help me! Help... Oh...
Talk to Patriarch Semer Knef in the cultists' camp.

Well then. I must admit, your help was right on time. We've accomplished a lot, you and I - my mind, on your legs. As far as I'm concerned, you would already be useful as a... Well, it's not important now. Please just relay my opinion to the Patriarch. Tell him that I am proud of you! And Grigori Domov's advice is worth its weight in gold!
We, the faithful followers of Sarn, know the true Revelation. We will share this with you. Some day. You have chosen the right path. History, as they say, is written by the victors. In our case, it is Nihaz. So how can one learn what truly happened? Eh? Easy! Ask the losers! This is something you must do as well: listen and accept Sarn's Revelation in your heart. But don't forget, assistant, everyone lies.

Do you think that Grigori Domov is too brusque? He's an amazing diagnostician, so we must be patient with him.
But now we need to talk to you about something else. Prepare yourself for a serious conversation.
Find Ignatius Chernov on the Bone Hill.

The only clue we've got is Ignatius. So let's see where he leads us. As far as I know, Nomarkh Ankh sent a group to the Bone Hill on some kind of mission. The group included Ignatius. He should be there now. No one has yet returned from the hills. Find him quickly and bring him here. Make sure you don't let on that we suspect him of something. The investigation has only begun. And may Sarn's light show you the way!
Ignatius's body... Looks like there's no one to bring back to camp, after all.
Yuck! What a stench! Stop. This person has infected many people with a strange illness. The illness appears to be passed on simply by proximity alone. Don't get too close to the body.
Return to the cultists' camp, report to Patriarch Semer Knef about what happened, then talk to Maria Zavetina.

I'll have to tell Maria Zavetina about the death of her first suspect. And I'll have to tell the Patriarch about his death, too.
Hey, what is this?
Were you able to find Ignatius? He is our only clue!

Dead?! Oh no! How can it be! What do we do now?
Ignatius was a tool of Nihaz! He accomplished his dastardly mission and left. How can we prove it? Or disprove it?
Run as fast as you can to Dr. Grigori Domov.

Stop! It's painful just looking at you! Some people already look better lying in their coffins... This is a... plague!
And you! Oh great Sarn! Another one! Quick! To the doctor!
Grigori is a well-known diagnostician. He promised to find the cure. Go straight to him, and don't lose another minute!
Hey, what's this? Idiots! I warned you! Don't go wandering around the ruins! Stay away from the corpses! Truly, as Sarnaut's population is increasing, its intellect stands still!
What's that? You're a corpse, that's what! Well, not yet, but you will be. You can crawl off to the barracks and sew yourself a burial shroud. Congratulations! The infection has reached you too.

I have bad news, and I have very bad news. Which would you like to hear first?
Well, it doesn't matter. I'll start with the very bad news. They're dropping like flies! Everyone who gets sick is dying! As for the bad news - you've got to help me. Otherwise, you're done for. But there is light at the end of the tunnel. Look at me - I am that light. The genius doctor, whose name resounds throughout Sarnaut. Or, resounds throughout what remains of Sarnaut.
Oh, damn that Nihaz, my leg... Again the leg. Yes, I'm complaining - quit staring at me like that. I've got an idea that we're going to try, you and I. Fly agaric mushrooms and concentrated sulphur - that's what I need. Well, that's what you need, rather.
These ingredients appear to be your only hope. Quick! Find them, you're our only patient still on his feet. Even if you have to crawl. Get a move on!

Don't panic! Dying is in fact easier than watching someone else die. Believe you me, I've lived through it all. Oh, so you don't want to die! Then you'll need mushrooms and sulphur - the genius cure I've discovered.
And here are the necessary ingredients. The story goes: "If you want to live, you better know how to hustle!" I understand...
Wait until the healing process is complete.

Well then, let's get to it! Mushrooms around here are saturated in the miasma coming from the Dead City, and when combined with sulphur and my know-how, the results should be miraculous! Good, so let's have those ‘shrooms, and I'll grind up this sulphur. What's your temperature? Fine. Stand still, I'll read the spell.
Close your eyes. No big deal here, it's not going to hurt, just a pinprick in your heel and a short gap in your memory. Brace yourself! You're very lucky to have fallen into Grigori Domov's hands. Don't forget to write about this in your memoirs, okay? Quiet, I'm going to begin.
What's this? Oh no! The leg was bad enough! Now I've got the plague, too!
Right, so the most important thing is to not miss a thing! The infection has reached me... That much is true. Give me a moment, I'm thinking. Aha! Hoorah for the thought process! I know what to do!

With the help of the amulet of sulphuric miasmas, force the shadow to enter your body. Leave the camp's boundaries and then, using the amulet again, destroy the cloud. Report back to Dr. Grigori Domov in the cultists' camp once you are finished.

This is no ordinary plague, this is a vile entity with its own evil will. It cannot be cured, but it can be killed! Along with the patient. Hah!
Don't be frightened. That was before. Before I figured it all out. I've just got a couple more creases in my brain than you, and look how much better mine works, eh? Brains of gold!
So now we'll modify the spell a bit... We'll add a few chemicals... A pinch of psi-salt... A dash of "pollen"... That's not for the spell, it's for me! We'll give it a try... Oh, the last batch was better tasting. But this one does the trick. My leg already feels a lot better! And now - to work.
Here's the amulet, which is full of the healing energy that chased the darkness out of your body. Although, if you ask me, it was the hydrogen sulfide... But no matter!
We'll smoke that vile spirit out. We just have to pick the luckiest warrior. Who have we got here? Just you and I. One, two, three! You're it! My mind is too vital to the world of science... We can't possibly risk it.
Well then, your job is to catch this black cloud and confine it in your body. You'll need the special amulet I created for that. I can't predict who the cloud is going to infect next. So you'll have to run, chasing it from one host to the next until it ends up inside you. As soon as you start to feel weak, this means that phase one is complete.
Then go a little further from the camp and try to drive the vile stuff out of your body. It won't have anywhere to go - it's not dumb enough to attack a squirrel or something. The darkness will leave you and then - get on it! It's all very clear to me, how it should go. What are you standing there blinking at me for? Get moving!

Aha, glad to see you again! To be honest, I hadn't much hope of seeing you among the living! The plan went something like this: "...If he doesn't survive the plague, then just try to dispose of the body somewhere far away from the camp." Yes. But all the same, I'm glad to see you!

There's been just one bit of good news in the whole time that you and I have been here. The plague shadow has been destroyed! Excellent!
 Grigori Domov - you're a genius! Wait a minute, don't go too far! We're safe now, but duty demands that we find out what's going on! And we need assistants! Ideally, ones with brains of their own.
Was I right? There's a summoner working over at the Watchtower?

Here are our Sparks. Well, not ours, but rather the draconids'. The Sparks infected by the plague, Sparks on the brink of death. In my favorite condition!
What do I think? It looks like the plague shadow is a parasite that latches onto the soul. It's goal is not to kill, but rather to infect the spark, to poison it and turn it into something resembling itself. The infection works like a chain reaction and soon the whole allod would have turned into a cloud... If not for my keen, perceptive mind, everything would have come to an end!
Wait just a moment, be quiet, don't move, and don't interfere. I must study the Sparks of the draconids and confirm everything.

Speak with Nomarkh Ankh to re-enter the spectral realm as a Spark and visit the Watchtower, the Rotten Ruins, the Wretched Corner, the Swampy Pass and the Palace Square. Report the results to Grigori Domov in the cultists' camp.

Well then. It's not quite how I had imagined it. But that was a hypothesis, while now I've reached a diagnosis.
Did I tell you what a great diagnostician I am? I think I did. So we discard the theory about parasites. This is no ordinary infection. The plague shadows establish control over the Sparks and then... They take them somewhere! Do you know what all this reminded me of? Tep! This all greatly resembles Tep's Plague. It's possible that the plague on Wandering Island and Tep's Plague are one and the same.
But where are the sparks going? They must be going somewhere on the island. But where? So, there's our answer - follow the shadows! Naturally, you'll need to get to where the shadows originate - ghostly world.
Needless to say, it will be you making the trip, not me. And how can we send you to the ghostly world where the essence of these shadows is located? I'll set your spark free - it's no trouble. For me that is. I'll give you a concoction to drink, and that's it. Your body will already be growing cold. Only I can't bring you back...
That's the only hitch. Go talk to our staff pathologist and amateur exhumer, Nomarkh Ankh. He once let it slip that he knew a way to free the Spark free from the body and then put it back. Don't worry. You body will remain here, safe and sound. And your Spark will be free!
Carefully search the ruins. My dear assistant, we're nearing a discovery. My fingers are shaking with impatience. Onward!

I myself wouldn't risk entering the spectral realm right now. I can only imagine what's going on there. But you've got nowhere else to go. And besides, if it hadn't been for me, your carcass would be all rigored by now, and as for your Spark... I don't even want to think about that!

Welcome back! Nothing like being back in the old flesh again, am I right? If only my damn leg didn't hurt so bad... Oh, how I'd love to have your body! Thunder and lightning, what pain!
But enough of that, tell me what you've learned. All the plague shadows are converging in a single spot? Just as I thought!
Meet with the Keeper of Knowledge at the Altar of Truth in the Master's Citadel.

Do you remember what the Spark of that mage you freed said about the Experiment? I can't stop thinking about it. What was the experiment? What were the goals and what were the consequences?
Did those mages of yours try to reproduce Tep's greatest spell?
Report all that you found out to the Keeper of Knowledge. Perhaps that knowledge will become another bit of the puzzle that will help us learn something new about the world.

An experiment? Let me think.
No, I'm not familiar with any such "Great experiments." At least, not the really great ones, in which the Great Mages died. Except perhaps the experiment on the Night of Astral Portals. A lot of the Great Mages died in that one, although they're basically immortal.
Wait a second. Couldn't that experiment we know so little about be the one that opened a path for the demons to reach our world? But if that's the case, how does Tep's Plague factor into all this? Could they be related in some way? Something gave the demons the strength to leave the astral for earth.
Nothing but guesswork and hypotheticals! It's too bad you weren't able to learn anything about the Experiment from the fallen mage. Moreover, we don't even know how long ago he died...
But in any event, thank you for telling me that story. I hope that in your wanderings you'll be able to learn more about that experiment. All of my experience is telling me not to discount this kind of knowledge!

Confirm to Nomarkh Ankh your willingness to help.

There you are. I was just thinking about how much I could use a capable, agile helper... Someone like you!
I can't promise you mountains of gold. Nor can I assure honor, glory, respect, or any of that other nonsense that heroes expect. The work will be dirty and it might stink. But the knowledge you gain in helping me in my research will be priceless.
I suspect that the appearance of so many undead on this island is the handiwork of one of the greatest summoners in the world. Maybe a young Tep getting his start! But you'd be reasonable to ask, what did the mad summoner need in the Dead City, and what magic generated such a phenomenal number of undead? If only we could find the answers to these questions... I don't know what it will give us, but I am sure that this knowledge will come in handy for you and your friends in your "understanding of the truth," as well for us.
So what will it be - would you like to advance the cause of science?

This is just dandy. I happen to be in need of a reliable assistant, whom I might send to the most dangerous places on this island. I myself never learned to swing the sword, nor can I wield magic. On the other hand, my powerful mind and your fighting skills would be quite complementary, and I think together we could unlock this ancient riddle.
Tell Nomarkh Ankh that you are ready to help.

Do you see this lunkhead? His pallor might be a little off, but he's the key to the secrets of the Wandering Island.
Right away I thought: who better to tell us what is going on here than a member of the local undead? The only problem is that these overly aggressive skeletons are refusing to speak with us. The desire to kill will only dissipate once their arms, legs, and head have been ripped off, and then they'll lack any means of communication. It's a vicious circle.
Then I decided to move a little faster, to make a creature that would obey me like child obeys a parent. Since it's made from the bodies of local undead, including, of course, their brains, it will have the necessary memories.
Well then, let me introduce you: this is Meathead. Don't expect a response, though. That's the problem. He's not finished. There's not much time, and I still need a lot of bones and flesh - the same dead flesh that's wandering around here in abundant quantities. Will you give me a hand?

Tep is my meal ticket! Two graduate degrees and a doctorate - these are not just scraps of paper.
You don't think I could put a spark into this heap of flesh and bones? Nothing to it! Give me the material and I'll turn modern science on its head!

And here are the parts. Excellent! Don't go too far. Give me a moment to sew everything in place, and then we'll both be witnesses to the greatest of secrets - the transformation of inanimate matter into a sentient being! Well then, let's get started!
Wait for the end of the reanimation ritual.

Right, so the body is ready. I barely had enough thread. Look at what a beauty we've got! He's a sculpture, not a warrior! We could send him straight out to the Palace Square to help our fighters. But Meathead has a higher purpose. He will serve science! We must discover all of the secrets of this island!
Right, the last step. I already put the spark into his chest, but it's still asleep. We only have to wake it up! It's not a complicated process. I did it during my dissertation. Granted, the members of the board did suffer a few injuries. But that was a long time ago. I was young and full of piss and vinegar then. This time everything will go perfectly. Look.
Did you see that? He started to move! Oh, my tough little guy! At times like these, I feel a genuine father's pride!
He is moving awfully slowly. His lips are hardly moving at all. I can't hear his voice. Yes, it looks as if we're not going to be able to talk with this one.

I know what the problem is. His Spark is too weak. It's been handled too roughly with all of the fighting and then being reborn. To be honest, I simply chose the one closest at hand. It was definitely weak. This can be fixed! We just need to fill his Spark with lifeforce.
And again I must recruit your help. Here's another amulet. This one is called "the Swallower," which speaks for itself. It absorbs lifeforce, soaks it up like a sponge. You'll only have to get close to a dying being to catch the Spark just as it leaves the body. You won't necessarily even have to kill the body yourself. It will be enough to walk around the battlefield with the amulet in hand and you will have it full to bursting. You'll see! Give it a try! The Swallower won't work on the undead, but there are plenty of other sources for Sparks around. What am I referring to? The draconids and wormfaces, of course! Just don't use any of those suicidal ones that fall on our fortifications. They won't work - too weak. You'll have to find more serious opponents. For example, how about the ones protecting the enemy camp?
Maybe the oaf needs a Spark from one of these regular skeletons. It needs a little more lifeforce!

Thank you! The Swallower is about to burst from all the life it's got! I can feel it.
Maybe it'll be hard to believe, but no one values or loves life as much as necromancers.
Talk to Meathead and report the results to summoner Nomarkh Ankh in the cultists' camp.

Now we enter the final phase. Thanks to the fresh lifeforce, Meathead has started to talk. His brain is working better and his basic instincts are starting to operate. I hope that his instincts won't tell him to destroy every living thing he sees! It would be hard to part with such a valuable specimen, the product of my many years of accumulated knowledge.
As soon as I'm finished, you can have a word with him. Try to keep your questions simple. Basic syntax, no subordinating conjunctions or any of that malarkey. You know what I'm talking about.

What is this? What did he say? Couldn't understand a thing!
What a complicated thing the brain is... Yes, it will take some work to get him going.

I worry that my work with Meathead is only just beginning. But we do have one finding so far - the local undead know very well who Tep is. I would not be surprised if he's walked in Tep's lands.
Unfortunately, all we've been able to get out of Meathead are these bits and pieces. You go ahead and continue your wanderings for now, but keep your eyes open. And look for traces of Tep!
Study the crypt that the golems are guarding in the Swampy Pass and report to strategist Punch the Furious in the cultists' camp.

I have received a report. Somewhere in the Swampy Pass we've found a guarded entrance. I'd bet my arm that it goes underground, into catacombs or a crypt. The walking dead built it, I'm sure of it! The wormfaces are way too paranoid about guarding that entrance... They even set up war golems to protect it!
Our guys didn't have the guts to get in there. Cowards! So that's why I'm giving you an order. Go in and see what the wily wormfaces have hidden underground.
Get to it! Forward, march!

They say that back in the day there was a local here, Zak, who could creep around golems. Probably just a myth. You'll never take a war golem from behind.
You're better off in front, and then just put him on his ass as soon as possible! Fists will solve any problem, hah!

Back already? Nice work! Tell me, what are they up to over there?
Supplies, ammunition, and captured women? No... What the hell is that? The black fragment. Hrm. What kind of crap is that?
Talk to Father Semer Knef in the cultists' camp, then return to summoner Nomarkh Ankh.

You mean that this rock was what the wormfaces were trying to protect? Who knows what this crap is. It's the first time I've ever seen anything like it. Take it away from here, please. It seems dangerous. It might blow up. Your sorcery will bring us to an early grave. Bring that cursed thing straight to Patriarch Knef, let him try and figure it out.
Well well, look at this! So you found a bit of black stone in the tombs?
I knew it! The traces of Tep that we've all been waiting for.
Go into the ghostly world and travel to the Palace Square. Summon Meathead with the Call of Flesh Totem, then defend him while he finishes his search.

Note that the wormface was summoning Sparks just like Tep did in his day, and their lifeforce healed his wounds. Where did he learn this? More importantly, where did he get the stone?
The Wandering Island is just a bit of earth and remnants of the Dead City. We might never have found this island, and it might have been lost in the astral depths, crumbling to dust. How did an artifact this strong end up here? What if Tep had experimented with immortality somewhere in these very ruins?
Hmmm... Let's try that as a hypothesis. We should go over the catacombs with a fine-toothed comb. You won't be able to pull it off yourself... I have an idea!
Meathead was created using the bits of Tep's knowledge that I was able to understand... That means there's a chance he might be able to sense the black stones. Do you see where I'm going? With his help we can find more fragments. I'll bet my own arm that there are more fragments here! By the way, this is a secret, but I once ordered a new arm for myself from the institute. I got the most advanced model, the very latest.
With some training, Meathead is already moving better and can follow orders. He's not much of a conversationalist, but that's not the most important thing, is it?
Here's the thing. I'll give you the Call of Flesh Totem and send you into the ghostly world. Your job is to go to the Palace Square and activate the totem. Meathead is a sentient creature. Well, he's getting there. This means he can also enter the ghostly world when summoned there by the totem. From then on out everything will be easy - follow him and protect him as necessary. He's still so weak...
Behind that door you'll find everything you need, mortal.

You won't believe me, but I'm thinking again. And a clear thinker is always a clear speaker.
Sometimes reality turns out to be more complicated than one might think...
Talk to Patriarch Semer Knef in the cultists' camp.

Behind those doors are all of the Wandering Island's secrets. But there's something more important here.
You are on your way to a new Revelation. To make the right decision, you should hear both sides, isn't that right? The God of Light has opened his mouth and is ready to speak. There's just one step left. Before you enter the catacombs - wake up! Return to your body and speak with Sarn's servant, Patriarch Semer Knef. The words he'll say will inspire you to look at things a little differently...
I see, Ankh was able to create his own Meathead. I'm not at all surprised!
Yes, I need to talk to you about one important thing... Where did you hear about that? I didn't even send scouts after you!
Destroy 5 fallen Sorcerers or Warriors around the Watchtower and then report to Semer Knef in the camp near the tower.

Oh, it saddens me to see that! A third attack fizzles out. It's no wonder this place is called Wretched!
Don't be surprised to see me here. It's just a projection of me. The Great Mages aren't the only ones who can be in several places at a time. But right now we have more important matters to discuss.
As soon as Dmitry leaves the captured camp near the Watchtower, the place will be overrun with the brainless undead. Cursed things!
It looks like we're stuck here. Dmitry is already sick of fighting the undead. We can't retreat, and we can't fight them... You're our only hope.
Clear the area around the tower of the undead, and maybe our commander will cheer up, and it will improve your reputation among the cultists.
Is the path to the Wretched Corner clear?

Excellent! We won. The fewer undead we have to deal with, the higher our chances of success. It will also improve your reputation. Perhaps it's time to begin the assault. At any rate, it's for Gromov to decide. Sarn be with you!
Destroy 5 pale undead around the Wretched Corner and then return to Semer Knef with a report.

Now, onward to the Palace Square!
Soon the warriors of Sarn will take it by siege. Goliath is coming from the west, and woe unto them who stand in his way. Here, in the east, we need to help Gromov. He'd be glad to attack right now, but he knows that the undead would just pour right in behind him.
To ensure that no one interferes with our commander's ability to crush the defenders of the Palace Square into smithereens, we'll need to clear the way.
You've already probably seen enough of the undead for a while. I myself don't quite understand where they come from, or how there got to be so many. Well, I must admit I have my guesses... We'll talk about all that some other time.
Annihilate the undead around the Wretched Corner and in the meantime we'll start preparing to assault the Palace Square.
What's the good word? What's happening around the Palace Square?
The more undead you kill, the better our chances of success.
Destroy 5 outcast mages or outcast warriors around the Palace Square and report to Semer Knef.

Thanks to your help, we were finally able to sweep our enemies from the island. I just worry that it might not be for long. There are too few of us to maintain control of the entire island. Soon we'll have to return to our camp.
But as long as we've still got the Palace Square, I've got a job especially tailored for your talents. There are undead inhabiting the ruins. More to the point, there are undead outcast mages and warriors just waiting for the chance to ambush one of our soldiers and tear him to shreds.
Every demon and every person would breathe a little easier if you spent a little time purging the area of these dimwitted creations who have nothing whatsoever in common with the noble Arisen.
Next time we attack, our warriors will have an easier go of it knowing that someone has already done something to protect our backs!
I've been trying to figure out where all these crowds of undead are coming from. Who summoned them? More importantly - why?
Nice job! Keep it up! Here's what I'll say in the report: "Our allies have destroyed a large number of undead around the Palace Square."
Destroy 5 undead on the Bone Hill. Report to Semer Knef in the cultists' camp.

Good thing we've got such excellent warriors as you on our side. It's too bad that the lies of Nihaz found you on your journey to the Truth before the good Word of Sarn. But there's still time, my friend... You'll have a chance to think about which side is better. But now - to battle!
When we last visited the Wandering Island, many of our comrades fell fighting the undead there. There's a reason it's called the Bone Hill.
The death of a warrior cuts a good commander to the quick. And Dmitri Gromov and Goliath are more than just good commanders. They're the best! Now, burdened by heavy thoughts and grief for the fallen, their faith in their powers might have been shaken... The church folk might have wanted to portray the demons as cruel monsters, but they are just as capable of feeling pain, insecurity, and grief during defeat.
Come on, show our warriors how the undead turn to dust under the fury of your attacks. Avenge our fallen comrades and fill our hearts with hope!
The death of our comrades is rough on me, too. Maybe in time you'll come to share my grief, when you become one of us in soul as well as body.

Victory!
Your first sortie, and you completed it successfully. Congratulations! I'll write it in the report: "With Sarn's blessing we've managed to purge the Bone Hill of the undead."
Destroy 5 undead around the Rotten Ruins. When the mission is complete, report to Semer Knef in the Rotten Ruins.

Nice to see a familiar face here! It's me, Semer Knef. Comfortable, no? And no scouts necessary. I can watch our progress from the camp. You'll see me again at various hot spots.
The wormfaces have faltered! Good job! But we've only just begun our journey. The road is blocked by the undead. Those blasted undead are all around us. We'll have to deal with those shambling beanbags before we begin our attack. Our warriors' spirits will rise after a difficult battle. For Sarn!
What's it like? What's the situation like around the ruins?

Are you done? Excellent! In my report to Goliath, I will write "I ask you to consider the possibility of organizing an assault on the Pass. The number of the undead has decreased considerably thanks to the brave and decisive actions of our volunteer assistant." Actually, demons cannot read, but superficial thoughts and emotions are perceived perfectly.
We must not hesitate! The sooner we drive the Wormfaces out of the Pass, the sooner we can get to portal to the Dead City!
Destroy 5 outcast undead in the Swampy Pass and return to Semer Knef.

We've come a long way already! Congratulations! But it's too soon to relax. The big push remains ahead. The Palace Square is the enemy's main stronghold. I can tell this is going to be a very difficult battle, Great Sarn, and we will lose many friends!
But there is a way to make things easier. All around the square are hordes of the undead. If we were to make our assault now and the attack lasted for a while, then the undead would block our ability to send supplies. You'll have to kill more of them. The less undead are left behind us, the easier it will be for our fighters to join the final and decisive battle.
Don't hold back! Spare not sweat, spare not blood! We stand on the threshold of victory! The portal is within our grasp! No retreat! For Sarn!
We'll clear the roads leading to the square. Then we can begin the attack!

Are you done with the undead! Praise Sarn! But don't begin the assault without Gromov - his forces should approach from the east.
Cultists, demons, and those who have found the courage to stand under our banner! Only together, only by joining forces, can we win!

With the help of the Amulet of Eternal Life, resurrect the fallen leaders of the wormfaces and draconids in the Wretched Corner, and the Swampy Pass. Defeat them and report to Semer Knef in the Palace Square when you are victorious.

There is no worse fate than to have to return to the battlefield day after day to die and die again. Tep, the greatest mage and madman of all time, knows this better than anyone else...
That's what the wormfaces deserve. Once they were humans, today they are monsters. Then there are the despicable draconids. And most of all, their leaders! They will beg for mercy, they will dream of peace and of the eternal compassion of the Creator. But they do not deserve our pity. Just as they showed no pity to us, children of Sarn.
It is a great honor to serve as an instrument of vengeance. Return the sparks to the fallen soldiers and then defeat them again. Are you prepared for this honor?
Die over and over. Be reborn and die again. Day after day! No end to the pain! Unbelievable suffering! The enemy has brought this upon himself!

To die a second time? To suffer, begging for mercy? That's nothing! They still haven't paid for what they've done! Tomorrow you shall return, and let the instruments of vengeance again rain down upon their heads!
Climb the stairs of the Sanctum and meet with Nihaz in the Alcove.

I...
I don't have the words to express the grandeur of Master's words. He is awe-inspiring. I swear that this world hasn't seen anything so amazing since the Great Nothing that preceded the creation of the earth and sky.
Oh, how I envy you, the Chosen One, Keeper of the Revelation. You shall meet with the Master as equals and you shall be shown the greatest secret of this world. A secret that only the gods know!
You will have the power to change this world forever. To remake it according to your will and desires. This is the greatest honor that a mortal could ever hope for.
Get to it. Climb the staircase and enter the holiest of holies, the Sanctum Alcove! The Master awaits!

You don't seem to be in a hurry. Has my booming voice turned your brain to jelly? It's happened before. What can you do? Being a deity is a double-edged sword. No one will take you seriously without all those absurd trappings of supernal power, dazzling feats of creation, and cryptic knowledge... Yuck! You know how sick I am of all that, after thousands of years?
In fact, everything is much more simple in real life. "If the mountain won't come to Nezeb, then Nezeb shall command goblins to build a new mountain." This is a local saying, but very relevant at this time, for we will create a new allod and erect a new portal to the Dead City on it.
I'll tell you up front that it's not going to be easy. In fact, it's going to be downright dangerous for you. But you don't appreciate things you haven't earned, friend, isn't that so?
Climb the stairs of the Sanctum and meet with Nihaz in the Alcove.

I...
I don't have the words to express the grandeur of Master's words. He is awe-inspiring. I swear that this world hasn't seen anything so amazing since the Great Nothing that preceded the creation of the earth and sky.
Oh, how I envy you, the Chosen One, Keeper of the Revelation. You shall meet with the Master as equals and you shall be shown the greatest secret of this world. A secret that only the gods know!
You will have the power to change this world forever. To remake it according to your will and desires. This is the greatest honor that a mortal could ever hope for.
Get to it. Climb the staircase and enter the holiest of holies, the Sanctum Alcove! The Master awaits!

You don't seem to be in a hurry. Has my booming voice turned your brain to jelly? It's happened before. What can you do? Being a deity is a double-edged sword. No one will take you seriously without all those absurd trappings of supernal power, dazzling feats of creation, and cryptic knowledge... Yuck! You know how sick I am of all that, after thousands of years?
In fact, everything is much more simple in real life. "If the mountain won't come to Nezeb, then Nezeb shall command goblins to build a new mountain." This is a local saying, but very relevant at this time, for we will create a new allod and erect a new portal to the Dead City on it.
I'll tell you up front that it's not going to be easy. In fact, it's going to be downright dangerous for you. But you don't appreciate things you haven't earned, friend, isn't that so?
Speak with Nihaz and listen to him carefully.

It seems that the time has come for a serious conversation. You are a quick study. There are few adventurers that could match you. But do not get cocky! You now stand at the beginning of a long journey which is itself the beginning of thousands of potential journeys. I wonder where your path will take you.
It's early to speak of this. We'll talk of something else...

Well then. Enough talk, let's get to work. Creating matter from energy is no easy task, and you'll have to do the work of ten. Of course, I will offer you my assistance, both materially and in the form of advice, but you will have to do most of the work. Otherwise, you'll never understand real power and remain easy prey for anyone with a deeper understanding of the astral, not to mention my eternal friend and foe, Sarn. Decide now - are you a powerless flea or do you have what it takes?
Charge the six substance generators and return to the Architect on the Citadel pier.

Now that you've got everything you need to create a new island, it's time to start. I shall call it the Cradle - since it is the cradle of your new power, the cradle of victory over our enemies. The cradle of the new world!
However, we haven't built it yet. There is just an area full of tiny bits of matter created by matter generators. I cannot explain to you exactly how it's done.
Now take an astral ship and get round the place where your island will be. Use your astralium to charge the generators I mentioned. It's simple as it goes: just take a piece of astralium to the generator's engine, and it will absorb its energy. The quantity you've got is enough for the six generators.
Be careful when flying in the area where new matter is created! If you deviate from the path, the energy that flows through the area will blast you into tiny particles!

Excellent. Construction is going as planned. I hope that we can finish it in time.
Bring more astralium right away - the generators are running out faster than I expected. I shall try to discover why the actual power is less than predicted during such high-energy expenditures...
Charge the 6 generators with astralium particles and return to the Architect on the Citadel pier.

Damn! I didn't expect the generators to consume so much astralium so quickly! It's like pouring astralium down a bottomless pit. Can it be that the scientists and laborers made a mistake during assembly? No, it can't be, I have already checked and re-checked everything myself.
What are you standing around for? Get back in your ship and charge up those generators with astralium. If the work piles up, then the unstable material will enter a borderline phase and the energy will change its potential... Let's just say that you'll hear the explosion all the way in your new home in the Purgatory!
Energy, energy... Where are we losing energy? We are expending more energy than was predicted and we're getting off-schedule!

What?? A generator has exploded? That can't be! It has three defense systems, all its essential components are doubled, all the fragile bits are well-protected, there's practically no operational wear and tear... How did this happen?
Damn it! Here's what we'll do. I will replace this blasted generator with a backup. You run and get some more fuel!
Charge the 6 substance generators using astralium particles and return to the Architect on the Citadel pier.

Well then. I was unable to explain why one of our generators blew up. It appeared to be a simple accident, a small mistake in the calculations. I gave my orders to replace the damaged generator and now we should finish the first phase of construction on time. That's assuming you'll stop standing there, gawping, and get busy recharging the generators.
Get back to your ship and get moving!
No problems this time, right? Piece of cake?

What?? Again? Not one, but several substance generators have all gone haywire at once? This simply can't be!
But what if... Ah yes, I've got it. Someone has been sabotaging our work.
Meet with the Architect on the pier at the Master's Citadel.

Now that you understand the scale of the task ahead of us, let's get to work. I am going to be a little busy, so one of my loyal and reliable servants will assist you during the first phases of construction of the new allod. He prefers to be called "the Architect." I've never understood why my disciples always go in for the most gaudy, grandiose titles... Tell me the truth, do I look "powerful and great" in this barrel-shaped body? So why the hell do all my servants bow and scrape before me?? That's one thing Sarn's got - he's clever. When he gave humans brains, curiosity, and a tendency to destroy, he made the perfect get-out-of-jail-free card for his prison. Now his cleverness has turned around to bite him!
But I'm getting off the subject. What can you do, I'm getting old... Haha!
Anyway. Go on, the Architect is waiting for you on the pier near the Citadel. I hope you two can work well together.

Let's see... You must be the piddling mortal that the Master was talking about? Yes... Looking at you, I cannot understand what the Master saw in you, what made him trust your feeble hands with such a powerful instrument. Why, that thing could send our entire universe ass over kettle!
Ah, I may have spoken too hastily. Don't be offended. It's just my pride and vanity. The faults of any creative type.

Sabotage! I swear to you, someone or something is dead set against us. The Master has many enemies in this world, and among them are those who would be capable of infiltrating our construction project. Oh, Master, why do you trust these adventurers? They clearly do not know how to hold their tongue!
Enough, this is no time for casting blame. We must do something or else we'll end up without any generators at all. Maybe it's time you got to work on this problem.
I'll give you a power cutter. It's not usually any good in combat. It's actually a tool for smoothing out rocky material on a construction site. However, if this kind of saw should run into any material object it will smash it into tiny bits!
Get in your ship and go back on patrol around the construction site. Find those damned saboteurs and grind them into astral dust!
I hope that by setting up regular patrols we'll be able to protect the generators from further sabotage. By the way, have you figured out who was behind that?

Let's see. Metal flying things that reminded you of Zem Blades? Very interesting... Could it be that the scientists from ZIT Headquarters decided to put a stick in our spokes? No, that's not very likely. The Empire is no longer our enemy, nor is the League for that matter. I doubt your good friend there would let a chance like this slip away... That's Tep I'm talking about!
Wait... I need to think.

Talk to the Architect and head for the Frozen Peak. Find out where Tep Cultists are stockpiling information about the Cradle, then destroy the cultist's camp with a tunneling explosive. Return to the Architect on the Citadel pier upon completion.

There! Now that I've had a chance to study the remains of the saboteurs, I know who we're up against. Moreover, I can even guess where they are hiding!
Those supposed saboteurs are actually reconnaissance drones! They gathered information about the substance generators and the principles of transforming the astral. The breakage started because of this interference in the generators' operation.
The drones are practically impossible to track, but for the fact that they don't have their own reactor and that their fuel capacity is exceedingly small. What does this mean? It means that they need somewhere to fuel up and drop off the information. This could only be one place! The Frozen Peak! It's a piece of icy cliff absolutely devoid of life. It was once the top of a mountain in Gipat. The explosion following the death of Tka-Rik sent a chunk of the mountain far into the astral. When we first arrived, we looked it over and, naturally, didn't find anything of value. So we forgot about it. It's the only spot that the cultists could set up a base on without us knowing!
I'll give you one of our most powerful explosives, the kind that I have exclusive rights to. It was created for peaceful tasks, such as smoothing out mountainsides. I want you to flatten the Frozen Peak. Find the cultists' information stockpile, where their recon drones are compiling information. Once you've found it, blast the whole thing to the astral demons! We won't see Cradle completed as long as the cultists are hanging around the construction site.
The cursed servants of a mad summoner! They have no idea what they're getting into. Interfering with the operation of such powerful forces could annihilate this entire section of the astral!

I saw a huge flash... I've always said that curiosity kills the damn cat!
The Master knows that the death of these stupid creatures saddens me. But their interference in the process of creating an allod could have had catastrophic consequences. It was thanks to you that this fate was avoided.

I heard the Harbinger of Retribution's report. Tep's minions got what they deserved! Knowledge must be earned.
Regrettably, these fools don't understand how they endanger us and themselves when they interfere in our work. More so now, when we've completed the first phase of creating an island and started the second phase.
But what can we do? Creation of an island is a process requiring constant work. We simply cannot halt construction and redirect our forces to defend against the cultists. We'll have to deal with both issues at once.
Take my power cutter, obtain an astralium particle and fly around our new allod. You can revel in your handiwork, while clearing the area of enemy mechanical spies.
How I hate when fools lay their clumsy hands on such delicate, complex machines! These substance generators are not toys! I'd like to impale the bastards on the screws with my own two hands!
Let's see the schedule... Whew, looks like it's fine. And yet something still worries me.
Talk to Nihaz, take over the astral body and pass the first barrier between the astral layers by defeating the astral guardian.

I see you are doing quite well. Well, how does it feel to be a demiurge, the creator of new worlds? Has quite an impact on your self-worth, doesn't it? Hehe. But don't get too full of yourself just yet. You've still got ways to go to become a true demiurge. Although, I must admit you're showing great progress. A few more millennia and you'll become almost like I was in my youth, haha!
Relax, I'm just teasing... You really are doing quite well. Perhaps I can even trust you with a more challenging quest.
As you know, the allod that we're creating in the astral already has its reflection in all the layers of the astral. However, the island is material only in this world, whereas in the deeper layers of the astral it is felt as a kind of "echo." It hasn't materialized yet, and it is easy to distort. And if you distort the reflection of an object in the deepest layer of the astral, then its true identity will be distorted in this world as well!
Why am I telling you all this? Because someone is trying to interfere in the creation of an allod by influencing its reflection. And it can only be Sarn! There's nobody else in this world who knows the principles of working with the astral, even your so-called "Great Mages"!
You'll have to deal with this problem. Your soul, as you know, comprises the astral body and a Spark. I can split your soul and send your astral body into the depths of the astral, where our enemy is hiding.
Barriers between the layers of the astral are protected by astral guards. In order to pass through to the second layer of the astral you have to defeat the guardian, and it will be a very difficult battle. When you feel that you are ready - talk to me.

The ability to divide your body into material and astral components is a gift that is only available to the chosen few. So far I know of only one of your world's inhabitants capable of this. And you know him as well. His name is Tep...

How are you feeling? Any noise in your head? Are you seeing stars? Hah, you're stronger than I thought! Many never even return to their body.
What if you were to suffer the same fate? Well, I would've been very disappointed in you, considering all the time and effort spent to open your eyes.
But you managed to overpower the guardian, and that is good. That means the astral has accepted you. Take a break, rest up, and we will continue our search.
While in the astral body, pass through the third layer of the astral by defeating the guardians of the barrier, then report to Nihaz upon completion.

I look at you and wonder. Where do mortal beings like you get such an inexhaustible thirst for knowledge, so much perseverance and persistence in achieving your goals? I reckon Sarn did well when he created your ancestors. If I had a hat, I would tip it to him. But the irony is that he will be destroyed by his own creation.
And now on to current events. Our enemy doesn't stop their attempts to hinder our work. So get ready to head into the astral in your astral body.
But this time you'll need to break through even deeper - at least the third layer of the astral - by defeating the guardians of the first and second astral barriers which separate the layers.

I see confusion in your eyes. You're probably wondering why I need all this: telling you about the astral body, learning to control it? But I am not going to tell you, hehe. If you can guess, good; if not, well, that's your problem. The ability to analyze facts is far more important than powerful muscles or even the most sophisticated magic. Believe me, I know what I'm talking about!

Ho! You're a veritable hero! Dealing with astral guardians isn't for everyone. These aren't demons that explode to bits from a single bomb; here strength of spirit is paramount!
Anyway, get some rest, astral combat will wear anyone out. In the meantime, I will check out how things are going with our allod.
While in the astral body, get as deep into the astral as you can.

Well, well. Our opponent isn't sleeping. The distorted region of space where the future allod is forming as we speak is becoming increasingly unstable. Someone or something continues to interfere in our affairs. Perhaps I might have to intervene personally. Still, the brunt of the work will have to be done by you.
You are no longer the feeble and helpless lump of flesh that had appeared in Gipat a time ago. You've managed to overcome many powerful enemies, more than even your Great Mages have seen in their entire long lives. And I hope that you will carry out my quest as well.
So, you will need to return once more to the deep layers of the astral. But this time do not stop! Go as deep as you can. Give your life if you have to, but break on through! Either we get to our enemy in the nearest future, or our allod-creating venture will fall through.
Hmm, the problem seems to be more serious than I thought...

Wow... I didn't expect that, oh no I did not. I blamed Sarn, but this development...
So, the Light is getting aggressive? It sensed power and attempted a power play? We'll see how that plays out...
Meet with the Architect on the pier at the Master's Citadel.

What are you staring at? What? Do you think gods can't make mistakes? Hah! Then Sarn would never have created you. And he wouldn't have bothered to butt heads with me, since he knew that he would lose, I know he did! But he was hoping for some miracle, which obviously didn't happen.
But the Servant of the Light is not someone you can tussle with at this juncture. Moreover, these aren't even your problems. I'll take care of that cheeky bastard myself. Oh, I'll take care of him so hard you'll see sparks fly! Tries his damnedest to pass for an angel, all the while pulling dirty tricks behind my back! No matter, he'll get his soon enough.
And you should go see the Architect. The island's creation is entering its final phase, and your assistance is very much needed.

I am delighted that we have solved our problems.
The last phase is the most difficult of all. There cannot be any mistakes!
I trust you have the astralium? Soon we shall need it.
Meet with Nihaz in the alcove of the Master's Sanctum.

The Master requested that you go to him immediately! He's waiting for you in the alcove of His Sanctum.
And make haste! You mustn't keep the Master waiting. Surely such an urgent call is very important.
There you are! Just in time. We ran into some difficulties, and your help is needed.
Board an astral ship and charge matter generators, then ask Nihaz about future plans.

I do not understand why the Master is in such a hurry? We won't even have the time to create water and clouds! Even breathing on that forming rock will be difficult!
We'll have to finish much of it on the Cradle itself, without matter generators, virtually by hand. It's not the worst thing in the world, seeing as I know how to turn a barren wasteland into a flourishing oasis, but how long will it take, huh? Why, oh why the Master bid us to complete the works right away? I can see it in your eyes that you know the answer.
No, no, don't say anything! If the Master wanted me to know the reason, he would have told me. Who am I to doubt the Master's wisdom?
But you... you are another matter! This land is intended for you and others who walk the path of Truth. So what use are these empty doubts?
Board an astral ship and go. The generators must be reconfigured and fueled with the energy that was scattered in the ​​construction area, and our work will be completed!
I'll give you an astral converter. It collects regular energy from the environment and redirects it to the generator. Charge the generators, then go see the Master. He'll tell you about our subsequent plans.

If it weren't for you, this would've been a failure. So much work... Aye, it has been too long since the Master has shown His truly divine power! Be proud to be a part of the great act of creation of new land!
While in the astral body, defeat Madness Incarnate in the Heart of Madness and return to the Keeper of the Universe.

Madness... It always follows in your tracks. You hide from it behind the wall of iron logic, citadels of common sense, but madness always finds a loophole. I have seen many renowned people that have endured countless blows of fate succumb to madness in the span of a moment. It is a miserable sight! What good are all their victories and accomplishments if they cannot even fathom their value?
Your next battle will be against Madness Incarnate. Remember that madness never comes out of nowhere. There are always manifestations of impending madness, and only by detecting them in time can you preserve your mind... and your life!
Go and only come back with victory!

I admit, I was afraid that you'd come back a helpless madman, without the slightest glimmer of reason in your eyes. I am glad to see my fears were unfounded. Having defeated madness that's always in hot pursuit of every great hero, you clearly demonstrate your Power of Intention.
With your desire incarnate, you are one step closer to the Dead City!
While in the astral body, defeat Cunning Incarnate in the Heart of Cunning and return to the Keeper of the Universe.

Cunning is a favorite weapon of your enemies. When you cannot tell your friend from your enemy, when at every moment you expect a blade to in your back, you are weak and vulnerable. But if you wish to win the battle, you have to understand the lessons of deceit: learn to lie, betray and backstab, spin a web of intrigue and falsehoods, toy with emotions, sic one against the other... No one will force you to do these things, but you will need to learn about deadly cunning - a weapon against which there's no protection.
Go into the Heart of Cunning. There the intentions of your enemies have collided. Who will you side with? Or will you deceive them both? Decide!
Go and only come back with victory!

Do you feel guilty about helping someone, and then turning your weapon against your recent ally? I think not. Circumstances are often such that a common threat unites even the most implacable enemies, but as soon as their misfortune passes, recent allies readily resume their acrimony. And only in your case, a betrayal of a one-time ally has turned against him.
He who plots treason may well become victim of it himself. Accepting the truth of that fact, you assert your Power of Intention.
With your desire incarnate, you are one step closer to the Dead City!
While in the astral body, defeat Chaos Incarnate in the Heart of Chaos and return to the Keeper of the Universe.

Any war is chaos. Unrest, confusion, discord, general distrust...
But chaos is much more than simply destruction. Chaos is the foundation of all things. If not for chaos, there would be no development, and the world would remain forever still. Order can tame chaos, and then at the converge of the two forces emerges a third, whose name is life.
You want to live? Do you want your friends, your brothers and sisters in arms, your entire peoples to live? Then tame chaos, which is carried by the Master's enemies into this world. And remember - only order can defeat chaos!
Go and only come back with victory!

Good! Taming chaos with order, you... no, you don't create a new life, don't worry - chaos incarnate is not quite chaos, for it has a certain order. However, by winning you demonstrate a clear Power of Intention.
With your desire incarnate, you are one step closer to the Dead City!
While in the astral body, defeat Spirit Incarnate in the Heart of Spirit and return to the Keeper of the Universe.

Spirit, soul. Debates over what it is have gone on for centuries. Some calls it a "breath of the Creator," but who created the Creators themselves? Others call it "the essence of life"... But many living creatures have no soul.
No one can offer an exact answer. We only know that the soul is essentially composed of a Spark and the body's energy aura, its "reflection" in the astral. And the soul can feel pain, too. Not physical pain, oh no, but emotional!
You shall soon meet Spirit Incarnate. Conventional weapons and magic will not harm it, for emotional pain can only be inflicted by another soul. I'll give you a hint - Spirit Incarnate can only feel pain from the death of its own Spark... Or the death of other Sparks nearby!
Go and only come back with victory!

Victory over Spirit Incarnate has strengthened your own spirit and clearly demonstrates your Power of Intention!
With your desire incarnate, you are one step closer to the Dead City!
While in the astral body, defeat Power Incarnate in the Heart of Power and return to the Keeper of the Universe.

Power... It is craved by every creature that's sentient and self-aware. To subdue nature and other intelligent beings to your will - this desire is as natural to us as breathing! Power is capable of opening horizons and bringing about new possibilities, but do not forget that power also corrupts. And absolute power corrupts absolutely. But you will yet see it with your own eyes.
Go into the Heart of Power and fight its manifestation. You will understand that those who have power care not for anyone but themselves, not even for their allies, friends and followers. And most interestingly, their power hangs on those who are willing to die for some illusory ideals. But when stripped of his followers and left on his own, the seeker of power is powerless!
Go and only come back with victory!

Well, now you know what power is and how it is dangerous. Look at the Master! His power is almost limitless, but he barely puts it to use. Have you ever heard him issue a stern order? Never! He always asks, persuades, calls on us to believe in ourselves and follow Him. He wishes for our understanding, not blind obedience. And that is why he chooses only those allies who have a powerful will of their own. Like you! After all, you can easily demonstrate your Power of Intention.
With your desire incarnate, you are one step closer to the Dead City!
Talk to the Keeper of the Universe and learn more about the Power of Intention.

You and other adventurers will travel from the Cradle to storm the Dead City. You need to go in a straight line by creating a portal.
The basis for the portal has been created, but activating it will require a lot of effort. You already know about the Power of Intention, yes? No? How come? You are fighting astral battles, learning the universe's secrets, but don't even know its basic laws? Truly, the creatures of this world are strange, indeed.
Listen carefully, and I will tell you about the Power of Intention, and how it can serve your cause or impede it.
Power lies not in muscle mass, not in powerful spells or sophisticated knowledge. Power lies in the sincere belief in your cause, in your abilities, in your Truth!
I rarely ever meet such an more attentive listener like you. I hope you will survive in the upcoming battle, and I will yet brighten up your solitude with conversation.
Bring 3 Desire Incarnates to the Keeper of the Universe at the Cradle.

It's time to start searching for the path. The straight path is not always the shortest, but for paths that stretch beyond this world, such as portals, this rule is entirely appropriate.
Every time you emerge victorious and confirm your Intention, the Power of Intention will manifest itself in this world. The Power of Intention is those very building blocks that will form your path to the Dead City. Fight the enemy's will while in the astral body, and achieve success doing so. Share with me your Power of Intention, and I shall open for you the first part of the path.
Strive, fight, harden your will. If you hate - hate, if you despise - despise. But make everyone respect your desires!
Yes! Look, the portal is coming alive! The first and most difficult part of the path is traversed. The will of your enemies is undermined, but you mustn't rest on your laurels.
Bring 3 Desire Incarnates to the Keeper of the Universe at the Cradle.

Your will is strong, Keeper of the Revelation. I would not want to be your enemy! You'll break through any barrier to carry out your plans, and woe unto anyone who stands in your way. In this you both resemble and differ from the Master. The Master's will is strong, but while you use it as a battering ram, the Master wields it as a rapier. You sweep away enemies from your way, while the Master... Oh, we should be talking about something else! After all, the work is not yet completed.
Keep trampling enemies with your Power of Intention. With each victory the winding path becomes shorter, and your goal closer!

Aye, it's been a long time since I opened any new paths. Opening a regular portal is easy, but paving a way is tough. After all, I'm sure realize that the issue isn't only whether or not you'll get to the Dead City, but also how you'll get there?

Excellent! Your current path is nearing completion. However, it leads not to a dead end, bur rather to a crossroads, whereupon a thousand more paths shall open to you. And it is only your will and your will alone that shall choose your path!
Bring 3 Desire Incarnates to the Keeper of the Universe at the Cradle.

We're almost there. Your enemies' resistance is nearly broken, and only pitiful remnants of a once strong Intention still oppose you. Smite your enemies, let your Intention and your desire for victory lead you! And when your Power of Intention completely subdues the enemy's will, the portal will come to life and the secrets of the Dead City will be laid out at your feet.
Know that even once you open the path, the battle will not be over. The only way to completely destroy someone else's will is by destroying its ​​host.

Yes! The path is open! Your Power of Intention has swept away all barriers. Now all you only have to do is give me an order, and I will send you to the Dead City.
But don't be in too much of a rush. If you continue to fight your enemies' desires incarnate, I will reward you generously for your victories.
While in the astral body, defeat Rage Incarnate in the Heart of Rage and return to the Keeper of the Universe.

It's time to demonstrate your Power of Intention in a duel!
This time you will go up against the base and animalistic emotion that is well-known to every soldier.
Go into the Heart of Rage, enter the protective dome and destroy Rage Incarnate. In a duel that's fair and one on one, your Intention must prevail against the beastly rage of our enemies!
Go and only come back with victory!

Good. You've managed to win, and by taming your own rage you were able to crush the enemy's. Keeping your emotions in check while in battle and resisting the pull of anger, you use the Power of Intention to defeat the enemy, turning his own rage against him.
With your desire incarnate, you are one step closer to the Dead City!
While in the astral body, defeat Thought Incarnate in the Heart of Thought and return to the Keeper of the Universe.

It's time to demonstrate your Power of Intention in a duel!
First there was word... No, first there was thought! And word came later, much later. Thought can cure and kill, create and destroy. If you wish for victory, your thought must be victorious first. Go into the Heart of Thought and defeat its manifestation!
Go and only come back with victory!
Good. You've managed to win the clash of intellects, proving your Power of Intention with the power of thought alone. With your desire incarnate, you are one step closer to the Dead City!
While in the astral body, defeat Death Incarnate in the Heart of Death and return to the Keeper of the Universe.

It's time to demonstrate your Power of Intention in a duel!
Death... Creatures gifted with the power of Light claim that you're not afraid of death. After all, there is no death for you, there is only a brief visit to the Purgatory. But in reality, deep within your soul you are all afraid of death, for there is always a chance that you won't be resurrected, and true death scares you more than anything in the world. But your enemies are accustomed to death. They have become one with it. And if you wish to demonstrate your Power of Intention, go into the Heart of Death and defeat its manifestation!
Go and only come back with victory!

There is no death! Death is merely transition between states of being. Now, having defeated Death Incarnate and thus demonstrated your Power of Intention, you understand this. With your desire incarnate, you are one step closer to the Dead City!
